The agent replied after taking it in (`data.excerpt`), or a lead call named it.

A stale source answered again; `data.source`, `data.staleMs`.

A project's chat got a message, or one of its messages finished streaming or had an inline item change state;

A project's chat started or stopped waiting on you, or its lead started or ended a turn; `data` is the

The app was focused on a project's screen with recent input, for one interval; `data` is

A machine_add started, moved a step or ended; `data` is `machine_setup::MachineAddStepData`.
machine_add_status reads the rest.

What a person may do on the hub. Owners and admins invite people, change roles and change hub-wide settings;
members work in projects. Each device is still capped by its own grants.

failing.description: The deciding check fails, rather than warns: with `look`, something can't work until it's fixed.

fields.description: What comes back from the provider, entered where the step says (`place`).

fieldsNote.description: What happens after the fields are saved.

fix.description: The deciding check's fix, when a command fixes it.

Where in the app the fields are saved, a Hub page of the app's Settings ("github"), where the terminal can't seal
them.

test.description: What Test does, in a few words.

way.description: The way in use, where a step has several: the one done, else the one that wants a look.

ways.description: The ways to complete it; one is enough.

why.description: Why it matters, in one line.

channel.description: Absent: the channel the hub's build came from.

machine.description: Retry this machine of the last run, whose hub updated: its node, then its Claude Code.

now.description: Update now: nodes restart without waiting for their agents to finish their step.

startOver.description:
Start over: ends the run going on, once the hub has its result (never while the hub restarts), with every part
left skipped, and starts a new one.

autoAt.description:
With `settings.auto`: when the build that is ready installs by itself, an hour after the last update started at
the earliest. Absent when nothing is ready, or automatic updates are off.

autoSkips.description:
With `settings.auto`: the build ready that automatic updates skip, as the hub didn't come up healthy on it and
it was put back; a newer build installs as usual, and Update still installs this one.

leftOver.description:
True when the run isn't finished but nothing in the hub drives it any more: it won't change again, and Update
starts a new one. Absent otherwise.

ready.description:
The channel's newest build, already downloaded and checked on the hub (and fetched by its nodes), so an update
only swaps and restarts: what "fleetd <version> is ready" names. Absent when there is none newer.

run.description: The update going now or the last one; absent when the hub never updated itself.

auto.description:
Updates install by themselves, at most once an hour: the channel's newest build an hour after the last update
started, whichever builds came out in between. Off by default.

drainMinutes.description: How long a node waits for its agents to finish their step, in minutes, 0 to 240; 0 doesn't wait.

HumanRequest.description: One human request, as stored and as every client shows it.

answeredByPerson.description: The person who answered it: approved or denied it, or entered the secret. Absent from a hub before people.

evidence.description:
What happened, in one line: "fingerprint ab12cd34", "exit 0 on devbox, approved by human:desk", or why it did
not run (and so is open again).

exitCode.description:
An approval that ran: its exit code (absent when a signal or the timeout ended it) and the end of its output,
with every injected secret value scrubbed.

its card into that checkout once. Only a person answers it, in every approval mode.

stdin and stdout. Its env adds to the agent's own.
MCP's streamable HTTP, with the server's headers on every request.
MCP's older HTTP with server-sent events, with the server's headers on every request.

McpValue.description: One env variable or header as the hub keeps it: a plain one's value, or the machines a secret's node holds it on.

sealedOn.description: A secret's: each machine whose node holds it. A project server's, its machine.

McpValueSet.description: One env variable or header of a server being saved.

oneOf.description:
The value sealed to each machine that runs the server: a project server's machine, or for a global one every
machine the app knows a box key of.
The secret already saved under this name, as it is: what editing the rest of a server sends.

MemoryCaps.description:
What memory writes are held to, in characters. A write past a cap is refused; a file already past a lowered cap
stays as it is until it is next written.

user.description: Each person's own memory (the shared `user.md` too).

topic.description: A project's topic file; absent for `user.md` and `MEMORY.md`.

projectRef.description: Also that project's MEMORY.md and topic files; absent: your own memory only.

caps.description: The hub's caps. Absent from older hubs.

files.description: With projectRef: MEMORY.md first, then the topic files by name.

projectChars.description: With projectRef: the project's files together, and their cap.

user.description:
Your own memory: how you work, read by the agents of work you start and by your Navi. Empty for a key with no
person. The one shared user.md on a hub from before people.

text.description: The other assistant's answer. Absent or blank: only the prompt.

added.description: Written to your memory, in the order they went in. Empty without text.

chars.description: Your memory's length after the import, and its cap.

prompt.description: The export prompt to copy, the same text every app shows.

skipped.description: Distilled but not written, and why.

MemoryImportSkip.description: Why an imported entry wasn't written.

oneOf.description: The memory already says it.
It held a key, token or password; `text` shows it with the value cut out.
No room left under the cap: the more durable entries (instructions and preferences first) went in instead.

MemoryImported.description: An entry an import wrote to the person's own memory.

replaced.description: The whole entry already there that it merged with and replaced.

MemoryNote.description: An entry `remember` wrote that is still in its file: when, and the chat line that said so.

MemoryRefreshJob.description:
The nightly memory refresh (hub/memory/refresh), listed with a project's automations as a built-in row: a hub job,
not an automation. Its hour is the hub's (`policy.memory_refresh_at` in `policy.tz`, set by an admin), its switch
the project's `memory_refresh` setting; it has no prompt to edit, no webhook and no delete.

lastRun.description: The run going now, else the last one.

MemoryRefreshRun.description: One refresh: when it started (or was skipped), how it went, and what it changed in memory.

added.description: Entries added, put in place of another, and removed: the "+a ~b −c" of its chat line.

state.description: running, done (it completed), failed (it didn't start, failed or ran past its hour) or skipped.

why.description: Why it was skipped or failed.
Why it didn't start; absent when it did.

MemoryRefreshed.description:
What a nightly memory refresh changed, as one line in the project's chat: each change with its own Undo, and Undo
all. Posted only when something changed.

items.description: In the order the refresh made them; the first [`REFRESHED_LISTED`] when it made more.

total.description: Every change it made, when that is more than `items` lists. Undo all takes them all back.

undone.description: How many of all its changes are undone, when any is: those past `items` too, which the line doesn't show.

oneOf.description:
The person's own memory: how they work across every project. One shared `user.md` on a hub from before
people.
This project's `MEMORY.md`, or one of its topic files.

personId.description:
User scope: another person's memory, only to delete it (empty text) once they are removed from the hub,
by an owner's or admin's device. Absent: your own; nobody else edits it.

text.description: The whole file. Empty deletes it (a topic's index line too).

topic.description: Project scope: a topic file; absent, MEMORY.md.

text.description: The whole file. Empty retires it.

item.description:
A "Memory refreshed" line's listed change, by its place in the line (0 first); absent, every change not yet
undone, listed or not.

messageId.description: The chat line that said "Remembered: …", "Forgot: …" or "Memory refreshed: …".

MergeRoute.description: How a landed change reached the default branch. The fixed order, bottom up on every chart, is the order here.

oneOf.description: A Change the merge train merged, batch members included: "Through fleetd".

Written by fleetd (a Change, a `fleetd/T…` branch or a task's head) but landed without the train: "Made by
fleetd, merged by you".
A merged PR with no Change and no fleetd branch: "Merged outside fleetd".

A first-parent commit on the default branch with no PR: "Pushed straight to the default branch". On a repo
whose git host fleetd can't read, a merge commit reads as a PR merged by hand and any other commit with no
fleetd trailer as pushed straight, so a PR squash-merged on the host reads as pushed straight there.

MergeRules.description: How the default branch may be merged into.

protected.description: Branch protection or an active ruleset applies to the default branch.

requiredReviews.description: Approving reviews a pull request needs.

rulesets.description: Active rulesets that apply to the default branch, by name.

squashAllowed.description: Absent when gh could not read the repository settings.

strict.description: Pull requests must be up to date with the base before merging.

MergedTile.description:
Pull requests merged per day: landed changes of all four routes over the range's calendar days (today as a
fraction, at least an hour).

previousPerDay.description: The previous period of the same length; absent when nothing was read that far back.

MetricsComparePeriod.description: The previous period of the same length, for the compare toggle.

MetricsCoverage.description: What the numbers cover and what they can't.

invisible.description: What fleetd can't see of the person's time, one plain line each, for the info sheet.

MetricsDay.description: One calendar day in the viewer's zone; days with nothing are present too.

notCounted.description: Bots and other merges not counted that day.

compare.description: Add the previous period of the same length's days (the tiles always carry its figures).

projectRef.description: Absent: every project you can read, each repo counted once.

days.description: Every calendar day of the range in `tz`, oldest first, empty days included.

merges.description: Landed changes in the range, newest first; `truncated` when there were more than fit.

repos.description: Without projectRef: one row per repo.

MetricsMerge.description: One landed change, for the list and the hovers.

batchPr.description: The train's batch PR it landed in.

firstPrAt.description: The stages between requested and merged: its first PR opened, its review passed.

projectRef.description: The project that owns it on this hub; the same repo may be checked out by others (`MetricsRepoRow`).

seenClaim.description: The ledger claim of a human session that saw this work before it landed.

sha.description: The merge, squash or pushed commit on the default branch.

touches.description: The person's touches that belong to this PR: reviews on it, its merge by hand.

MetricsRepoRow.description: One repo's four numbers, for the cross-fleet table under "All projects".

projects.description: Every project on this hub with it checked out, so the same merges show under each.

spark.description: Merged per day over slices of the range.

MetricsTiles.description: The KPI row: all four, equal.

ModelSource.description:
Where the model list came from: the Models API on the hub's API key, or fleetd's own list of current Claude
models.

NaviApprovalMode.description:
How a Navi's risky actions are approved (W239, D263): its sends, replies, shares and invites through an
integration, and a site it opens on its own for the first time. Whatever the mode, moving money, trading and
placing orders are refused, and so is a credential in outgoing content.

oneOf.description: Every risky action asks the person on a card; no checker runs.
A fresh checker model judges each risky action first: go runs it, ask brings the card, block refuses it.
Nothing asks and no checker runs: every risky action runs, past the hard floors.

NaviApprovals.description: A Navi's approval settings: its mode, and the checker's model and effort.

defaults.description: Whether model and effort are the hub's defaults, not a pick of the person's.

model.description: The checker's model: the person's pick, else [`CHECKER_MODEL`].

effort.description: The checker's effort; absent: the hub's default.

model.description: The checker's model; absent: the hub's default.

archived.description: False brings an archived Navi back. Default true.

NaviAsk.description:
One ask in `navi_asks` (the app's read of a Navi's asked work): where it went, its words, and the orders opened
for it.

text.description: The Navi's words, without the line telling the lead about the handle.

NaviAskOrder.description: An order opened for an ask, as it stands now.

headline.description: The lead's latest one-line headline for it.

NaviCard.description: The card a Navi pays with: a Credit Card item in its person's 1Password. Only the reference is kept.

card.description: A Credit Card item, `op://<vault>/<item>`, as onepassword_cards lists it; absent: the Navi has no card.

machineId.description: Where it lives; absent: the best worker (see `project_discover.best`).

name.description: What the person calls it ("Ada", "Home", "Taxes"). Its folder is named after it and keeps that name.

machineId.description: Only those on this machine; absent: every machine.

card.description: Absent until the person picks one: the Navi can't pay until then.

name.description: Its new name; its folder keeps the old one.

NaviSandbox.description: What a Navi's OS sandbox is on a machine, in a person's words.

fix.description: What to run to close a gap or make Navis run here.

line.description: "Navis run in bubblewrap, with abstract sockets scoped (Landlock)."

NaviSite.description: A site a Navi fetches and opens without asking: a person approved its first visit.

site.description: Its host, without a leading `www.`: `example.com`. Its subdomains are sites of their own.

sites.description: What it may still fetch and open unasked.

NotifyPolicy.description:
When a client may interrupt the human with an event marked `attention`. Quiet windows are absolute times the
hub computes from `policy.quiet_hours` in `policy.tz`: the one under way (if any) and the next.

coalesceSec.description: At most one notification per this many seconds; what arrives meanwhile is folded into the next.

quiet.description:
Only "urgent" events notify inside these; empty when quiet hours are off. Ask again after the last one ends
or on decision.recorded.

OnePasswordCard.description: A Credit Card item a person's 1Password token reads, for the Navi's card picker.

machineId.description: Where to list them; default: the first machine online that holds the token.

navi.description:
The Navi the card is for: listed on its machine with the token its fills use (its own
OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN variable, else the caller's).

error.description: Why none could be listed, the token masked; absent when it worked.

token.description: The caller's saved token; absent until they save one.

sealed.description: The caller's service account token sealed to each machine agents run on.

missingOn.description: Machines whose node doesn't hold it (offline when it was saved): save it again while they are online.

OnePasswordTest.description: The last Test of a token: the vaults it reads, listed with the 1Password SDK on one machine.

error.description: What went wrong, in plain words with the token masked; absent when it worked.

vaults.description: The names of the vaults it can read.

machineId.description: Where to try it; default: the first machine online that holds it.

OnePasswordToken.description: A person's saved token: never the token, only where it is.

sealedOn.description: Each machine whose node holds it. Work on a machine missing here has no token from the person.

OrderCard.description: One order (workstream) as the board shows it.

lanes.description: Active first, then newest; finished lanes are left out on the board.

settled.description: Agents done, failed or cancelled, of `total`.

decisions.description: Active decisions scoped to it. Absent from older hubs.

lead.description: Its project's lead (shared by every order of the project); absent when the project has none.

requests.description: Its open secret and approval requests.

steers.description: Its steers (to the lead or one of its tasks) with their receipts, newest first. Absent from older hubs.

workstream.description: Its record: the brief and its done-when. Absent from older hubs.

OrderPhase.description: An order's phase: the first match in this order wins, and the board sorts by it.

oneOf.description: An open ask for it, or a lane waiting on a permission.
An implementer or reader lane starting or working.
A Change reviewing, or a reviewer or qa lane working.
A Change ready, rebasing, in CI or merging.
Only queued lanes.
Draft, or running with no tasks while the lead works.
Anything else open: waiting for the lead.

OrderToMergedTile.description: Time from order to merged, over the landed changes that belong to an order (`train` and `fleetd_by_hand`).

fromOpened.description: Of `n`, those timed from when the lead opened the order rather than when the person asked.

noOrder.description: Landed changes with no order (`outside`, `direct`), shown as "n merged with no order".

prOpenMedianMs.description: PR opened to merged over every PR of every route, for a like-for-like comparison.

orders.description: By phase, then most recently updated.

code.description: `XXXX-XXXX`, single use: entered in the phone's pairing screen with `hubUrl`.

hubUrl.description: Where the phone reaches the hub: never a loopback address.

PatchId.description: Full lowercase hex patch id, 40 or 64 characters

devices.description: Human keys, each with its person, oldest first; revoked ones left out.

me.description: The caller's person; absent for an agent key.

PeriodBreakdown.description: The numbers of one period, for a comparison.

removedAt.description: Removed people keep their id and name, so what they did still names them; their devices are revoked.

choice.description: Absent: their subscription once connected, else the hub's API.

mayUseHubApi.description: Whether the hub's API is theirs to use: it is set up, and they administer the hub or members may use it.

runsOn.description: What the orders they start, and their Navi, run on now.

PersonGithub.description: One person's GitHub, as an owner or admin sees it on People: absent `account` until they connect.

PersonRef.description:
Who did something, with their name at the time: on chat messages, approvals, secrets, decisions and checklist
changes.

Placeholder.description: A `{{name}}` the code fills in. A required one missing from an edit gets a warning.

PrAuthor.description: Who wrote the PR: fleetd's agent when one did, and the GitHub account it was opened from.

laneId.description: The writing agent's lane in the agents view.

login.description: GitHub login; absent when GitHub wasn't reached.

PrBlock.description: A pull request: the client fills in its live state (title, checks, review, merged) from the hub.

title.description: Shown until the live title is known.

PrCheck.description: One check run or commit status on the head. fleetd's own merge statuses are left out: `queue` says the same.

PrChip.description: One PR on a train strip.

position.description: 0-based; absent for the head (being rebased, checked or merged) and for PRs merged today.

nextOffset.description: Pass back as `offset` for the next page; absent on the last.

noDiff.description: GitHub shows no diff for this file (binary, or too large).

diffLines.description: Lines `pr_diff` pages through; absent when GitHub shows no diff for it (binary, or too large).

path.description: Repo-relative; the new path of a rename.

headSha.description: The head these files are of.

nextOffset.description: Pass back as `offset` for the next page; absent on the last.

body.description: The PR's description, at most 8000 characters. Secrets are replaced by `[secret]`.

history.description: Its moves through the merge queue, newest first.

reviews.description: Newest first: agent verdicts and people's reviews.

mergeCommit.description: The squash commit on the base, once merged.

githubError.description: GitHub couldn't be reached: the list holds only the PRs fleetd records, without checks. Why, and what to do.

nextCursor.description: There are more rows: pass it as cursor for the next page.

PrQueue.description: Where the PR stands in fleetd's merge queue. Absent from a PR fleetd doesn't land.

length.description: PRs waiting in the same queue.

position.description: 0-based place in the queue; absent when not waiting in it.

reason.description: Why it is held or was sent back: a conflict, failing check names, or the refusal's fix.

PrQueueStep.description: One move of the PR through the merge queue.

position.description: 0-based place in its train's queue; absent when not queued.

reviewsDone.description: Clean reviews of the current patch.

reviewsNeeded.description: One for every PR the train lands.

taskId.description: The task that opened it (its writer), when the hub knows: the board groups the PR's checkers under it.

PrReviewEntry.description: One review: an agent's verdict with its findings, or a person's review on GitHub.

agent.description: The reviewing agent (reviewer or QA); absent for a person's review.

blocking.description: Findings that must be fixed before merging; agent reviews only.

current.description: It reviewed the PR's current change (an agent review stays current across a rebase that changes nothing).

login.description: GitHub login of a person's review.

text.description: The agent's findings, or the person's review text. Secrets are replaced by `[secret]`.

PrRow.description: One PR as the list shows it.

title.description: GitHub's title; the writing agent's task title when GitHub wasn't reached.

workstreamId.description: The work it belongs to, when fleetd's agents wrote it.

Profile.description:
One task profile (Settings › Hub › Every project › Profiles): what an agent on it runs on. Exactly one is the hub's default, which
every project allows and the lead, every review and claude's helper calls run on.

fast.description: Claude Code's fast mode (`fastMode`), only on a model that has it.

note.description: What it is for, in one line; the lead reads it to pick one.

refused.description:
Set by the hub: claude refused `model`, so its agents run on the runner's own model until a person sets the
model again. What claude said, and where.

ProfileModel.description: A model a profile may pick (`profiles_list`).

fast.description: Claude Code offers fast mode on it.

ProfileTotal.description:
One task profile's part of a scope's agent time and usage, from the spans kept (`coverage.detailSince` on): the
tasks that ran on it, and the lead's spans under the default profile they ran on.

outputTokens.description: What the runner reported for its messages.

default.description: True makes it the hub's default; the default can't be unset, only replaced.

model.description: Setting the model again clears a refusal.

name.description: A rename: the tasks not yet ended move to the new name; ended ones keep the old in their history.

projectRef.description: A project: also which profiles it allows.

allowed.description: With projectRef: the profiles it allows, the default first.

efforts.description: Every level Claude Code's `--effort` takes; a model without one runs the nearest below.

models.description: The models a profile may pick.

profiles.description: The default first, then by name.

create.description:
Make a new folder for the project first: at `path`, else `<projectsRoot>/<name from title>`. An empty folder
already there is taken; one holding anything is refused.

gitInit.description: With `create`: `git init` the new folder. Absent: a plain folder with no git.

useExisting.description: With `url`: when the destination is already a checkout of the same repository, add it instead of failing.

addId.description: A clone was started: its `project.clone_progress`, `project.added` and `project.add_failed` events carry it.

clone.description: A dry run with url: where it would clone, and whether that folder already holds a checkout.

created.description: False when the directory was already a project (it is renamed when a title is given), and in a dry run.

inspect.description: For a path, at once; for a clone, on `project.added`; for a dry run, the repository's facts.

path.description: The project's directory (the clone's destination for a url).

projectId.description: Absent while a clone runs: `project.added` carries it.

avatar.description: The picture's id, as the project's summary names it in `avatar`.

attachmentId.description: The picture, uploaded with attachment_put (png, jpeg or webp). Absent removes the picture: the letters again.

crop.description: The square of it to keep; absent: the largest square in its middle. Clamped to the picture.

ProjectChatState.description: One chat's state, for the sidebar and the status row.

lastSeq.description: The newest message's `seq`; 0 for an empty chat.

needsYou.description: The lead's last message waits for a human reply, or an inline item is open.

nudges.description: The nudges still waiting to be seen, oldest first: what the app shows as "N to look at". Absent when none is.

openItems.description:
The inline items still open, oldest first, however far back: the chat may not have their page loaded. Absent
when none is (and from older hubs).

ProjectCreator.description: The key a project was created with: its id, and the person's or device's name the key carries.

machineId.description: Scan only this machine; absent: every machine.

best.description: The machine a clone goes to by default: online, runner ready, fewest running threads. Absent: none is.

set.description: Variables to add or replace; a secret replaces a plain one of the same name and the other way round.

ProjectEnvVar.description: One of a project's variables as the hub keeps it. A secret has no value here, only its fingerprint.

bytes.description: The value's size in bytes, a secret's too, for the project's total ([`ENV_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES`]).

fingerprint.description: A secret's: the first 8 hex characters of sha256 over its value, as the node computed it.

query.description: Without projectId: only projects whose title or path contains it.

ProjectGetOutput.description: The projects, or one project's outcome (its fields at the top level).

profiles.description: The profiles its agents may run on (`project_set`), the hub's default first; absent from older hubs.

taskCounts.description: Absent until the project has a task.

threads.description: Newest activity first. Task threads are left out; they show under `tasks`.

trains.description: The merge trains of the project's repos; absent until one of its PRs was enqueued.

truncated.description: True when `threads`, `workstreams` or `tasks` was trimmed to its limit.

workstreams.description: Open workstreams (not done, stopped or failed), newest first.

ProjectIcon.description:
A built-in icon: a glass being with a face of its own, on a round field of a color. The apps ship each one as
images (app/shared/bot-icons builds them).

ProjectInspect.description: What a project's checkout or repository says: the default branch, CI and merge rules, and one line on what the lead will need.

leadNeeds.description: One line for a person, e.g. "no CI found: the merge train holds its PRs until the repo has CI".

notes.description: What could not be read, e.g. "branch rules need admin access on acme/storefront".

repo.description: Absent for a checkout without a GitHub remote.

ProjectKind.description: What a project is. Absent on a project: one of code, a lead with its repos and folders.

oneOf.description:
A Navi: a personal assistant in a plain folder of its own, whose lead runs the `navi.start` prompt in the
assistant role (`SessionRole::Assistant`).

ProjectProblem.description: Why something could not be done, and the one step that fixes it.

oneOf.description: The machine's node is not connected.
No connected machine runs agents.
gh is missing or logged out where it ran.
gh is logged in but cannot see the repository (private, renamed, or a typo).
The path does not exist on the machine.
The path exists but is not a git checkout.
The clone destination exists. `CloneTarget.sameRemote` says whether it is already this repository.
git clone failed; the message is git's own last line.
The machine's node is older than this hub and cannot do this.

ProjectRef.description:
A project: a workspace with a lead and its own directory, on its home machine, where the lead runs. Its
`projectId` is the node's id for that directory, so the ref also addresses the files; the directory may be a git
repo or a plain folder. A project holds zero or more repos (`ProjectRepo`), each in a node directory of its
own or in the project's.

removeWorktrees.description:
Also force-remove the fleetd worktrees its agents worked in, uncommitted changes and all, once its agents have
stopped. Their branches and the checkout stay as they are.

base.description: The branch its work lands on; absent until fleetd knows it.

checkout.description:
The node's directory holding its files: the project's own `ProjectRef` when the project's directory is this
repo.

path.description: The checkout's directory on its machine; absent before its node reported it.

repoKey.description: Its origin remote, shortened; absent for a repo with no remote, or before fleetd has read it.

name.description: Absent: from its remote or folder, e.g. `api`, made unique in the project.

path.description: A git checkout on the project's machine.

url.description: A GitHub URL, `git@github.com:o/r.git`, or `owner/repo`, cloned onto the project's machine.

useExisting.description: With `url`: when the destination is already a checkout of the same repository, add it instead of failing.

addId.description: A clone was started: its `project.clone_progress`, `project.added` and `project.add_failed` events carry it.

archived.description: The project the checkout was until now, archived read-only.

path.description: The checkout's directory (the clone's destination for a url).

repo.description: The repo, once added; absent while a clone runs.

repos.description: Oldest first, its own repo first; none for a plain folder.

ProjectRowState.description: What a project is doing, in one word.

oneOf.description: Agents are running, or its PRs are in review, CI or the train.
The lead is waiting for your reply.

Something outside the work stops it: its machine is offline, or at its usage limit or short of disk or CPU for
new agents. A red main is not one: the train keeps merging (`warning`).
Nothing running and nothing waiting.

profiles.description: The profiles it allows now, the default first.

env.description: Its agents' variables, by name. A secret's value is never here.

memoryRefresh.description:
True (the default): each night the lead tidies the project's memory, with a line in the chat to undo it.
Absent from older hubs.

repo.description: The repo `setup` is for; absent when it is the project's, and from older hubs.

setup.description: What runs in each new worktree before its agent starts; no commands when none are set.

worktrees.description: From the node, now: absent while it is offline or too old to say.

repo.description: The repo whose setup to read (its own, else the project's); absent: the project's.

memoryRefresh.description: Turns the nightly memory refresh on or off for the project.

repo.description:
The repo whose own setup to set, an empty one giving it the project's; absent: the project's. Title is the
project's either way.

setup.description: Replaces the project's setup commands and their settings; no commands turns setup off.

title.description: The project's name in fleetd; its folder keeps its own.

ProjectStatusRow.description: One project on the Status screen: a state word, its work in groups, agents running and the last merge.

agentsRunning.description: Its task agents holding a slot now (the lead's own turn is not one).

blockedReason.description: Blocked only: why, in one line, for the expanded row.

items.description: Group by group in `StatusGroup` order, newest first in each, at most `STATUS_ITEMS_PER_GROUP` per group.

merged7d.description:
Landed changes on its repos over the last 7 calendar days in the hub's zone, today included, by every route
(metrics_get's count). Absent when the metrics know none of its repos, so nothing is read as zero.

stale.description: Set when a source the row reads (its machine, its repos on GitHub, their merge train) went quiet.

throughFleetdPct7d.description: Of `merged_7d`, the share the merge train landed, in percent. Absent when nothing landed.

usagePausedOn.description: Blocked by a usage pause on this machine's login: the app offers Resume (usage_resume) for it.

usagePausedReason.description:
With `usage_paused_on`: the pause in its own words ("paused until Sun 23:40 UTC (usage limit on devbox's
login)"), which `blocked_reason` may not be when the machine is also degraded.

warning.description:
Worth knowing, but it stops nothing: a check red on main, and whether a fix is under way ("`ios sessions` is
red on main, fix in progress"). Any state.

message.description: The system line it wrote into the chat.

archivedAt.description:
A Navi's: when it was archived. An archived Navi keeps its chat, memory and folder, and its lead doesn't
start until it is brought back (`navi_archive` with `archived: false`).

avatar.description:
Its picture's id, from the hub, once a person gave it one (`project_avatar_set`): it changes with each new

parked.description: M4: its thread hit a usage limit; the task is idle until fleetd sends "continue" at `resumeAt`.

paths.description: The files the lead said a writer will change (`spawn_agent` `paths`), matched against later work.

pr.description: The PR a review task reviews. Required at spawn for review; absent on older rows (hub-spawned judges).

previousThreads.description:
The threads it ran in before `threadRef`, oldest first: fleetd restarted it fresh (its context filled up, or its
thread could not resume), on the same branch and worktree.

profile.description:
The profile's name, resolved at spawn: the spawn's, else the hub's default. It keeps the name it ran on through
a rename. Rows stored with a model and effort read as `high` (the hub migrates its own).

queuedReason.description: Why it is queued, e.g. "fleet cap: 40 of 40 running".

recovery.description: Set once a run of it died (its node stopped, its process was killed, a stall) and fleetd resumed it or will.

repoId.description: The project's repo it works in; absent for the project's own directory, and on rows an older hub stored.

TaskCounts.description: A project's tasks by state, all time.

TaskKind.description: Every task gets its own worktree: a writer on its own branch, a reader or reviewer detached.

TaskRecovery.description: A task fleetd resumes on its own after its run died: in the same thread and worktree, with a note to continue.

count.description:
Automatic recoveries used of `max`; a resumed run that died again before doing anything counts twice. A node
going away never counts here.

lastCauseText.description: The same, in plain words: "the node on devbox stopped", "the agent was killed by signal 9".

nextAt.description: When the resume goes out; absent once it has.

nodeLost.description:
Resumes after its node went away (stopped, upgraded, crashed, powered off): not the task's doing, so outside
`count`, with a high ceiling of its own only so a node that keeps dying can't loop it forever.

resumedAt.description: When the last resume went out.

signature.description:
What tells one death from another (its cause, exit and last tool); the same one twice is not resumed again.
Cleared when the lead continues the task itself.

streak.description: Deaths in a row with this signature, the latest one included.

endCause.description:
Why its last run ended (the node stopped, the agent exited, a limit, context full, …); absent on results an
older hub recorded, and when it never ran.

tail.description: The latest assistant message, trimmed to its last 2000 characters.

TelegramBot.description: The bot, as Telegram's getMe and its profile photo describe it.

photo.description: Its profile photo, small, as a `data:image/jpeg;base64,` URL; absent when it has none.

TelegramBridge.description: A Navi's bridge as the tools show it: never the token.

fingerprint.description: The token the Navi's node holds, by fingerprint.

offline.description: The node is offline: what the bridge shows is what it last said, and nothing goes through it now.

paired.description: Absent until the person pairs their account.

status.description: Absent until the node has said how it stands.

bridge.description: Absent until a bot token is saved.

link.description: `https://t.me/<bot>?start=<code>`: Start there pairs the account that presses it.

TelegramPerson.description: The Telegram account the Navi answers.

name.description: Their first and last name on Telegram.

username.description: Without the @; absent when they have none.

sealed.description: The bot token, sealed on the client with crypto_box_seal to the Navi's machine's boxPubKey.

oneOf.description: Asking Telegram for the first time since the node started or the token changed.
Reading Telegram: messages come in as they are sent.
The person paused it: nothing is read or sent until they resume.
Telegram failed or asked it to slow down: it tries again at `retryAt`.
It can't go on until a person acts: the token was revoked, or another program reads this bot.

TelegramStatus.description: How the node's bridge stands now.

error.description: The last thing that went wrong, in plain words with the token masked.

bot.description: The bot Telegram answered for, when the token works.

error.description: Telegram's words when it doesn't, the token masked.

model.description: The model the failure names, when the runner read one off it (a gateway with no account for it).

effort.description: As reported by the runner; not narrowed to Effort because it may report other levels.

endCause.description: Why its latest run ended; absent while it runs and from older nodes.

headline.description: First line of the latest visible assistant text.

focus.description: The index of `itemId` in `items`; absent when the node no longer has it.

pct.description: `train` over all landed changes; absent when there are none.

byProfile.description: Most agent time first; absent when no task or lead span is in the period.

storedBytes.description: The hub's span tables on disk.

nextAfterId.description: Absent when there are no more.

person.description: The person who last ticked or changed it, on an older hub; absent when the lead did.

Tokens.description: Summed over the lane's runs. `live`: the running run's usage is streaming in (else it updates at each run's end).

ToolAction.description: What an asking tool would do, for the card's heading and its urgency.

oneOf.description: Reaches another person: an email, a reply, an invitation or an answer to one.
Changes something of the person's: a draft, a label, a page, a document.
Removes something: a message, an event, a page, a file.
Gives someone else access to something.
Pays or buys: money leaves the person's account.
A Navi's final Confirm or Submit click on a site (`confirm_step`): a booking, a cancellation, a form sent.

ToolPermission.description:
An approval raised by a session's tool permission prompt instead of a gated command: answering it answers the prompt
on the project's node. Its machine is the request's project's.

checker.description:
A Navi's approval checker judged it before it reached the person (W239): why it asks them, or why it refused
it. A blocked prompt was already refused on its node; approving it anyway lets the Navi run exactly this input
once, when it asks again.

input.description:
The tool's input exactly as the session asked (at most 64 KiB of JSON): approved, the tool runs with exactly
this. Absent when the node didn't send it; the tool then runs with what the session asked.

preview.description:
An integration's asking tool (`hub/integrations`): exactly who it reaches and what it says, or what it changes,
read from the input it runs with once approved. Boxed: it is large beside the prompt's other fields.

screenshot.description: A Navi's `confirm_step`: its screenshot of the page, the project's, for the card.

site.description:
A Navi's first fetch or browser visit to this site (its host, such as `example.com`): approved, the Navi may
fetch and open it without asking from then on, until a person revokes it (`navi_site_revoke`).

summary.description: The command, the path, or the tool's own description.

ToolPolicy.description: The hub's policy for one tool.

oneOf.description: Reads: runs without asking.

approved.

A task or lead whose thread hit a limit; fleetd sends it one "continue" at `resume_at`, or at `check_at` to see
whether the login has capacity again, or (no reset named) as soon as another turn on the login succeeds.

checkAt.description: A limit that named no reset: when fleetd next tries the thread, 1, 2, 5, 10 and then every 15 minutes.

proxy.description: A proxy in front of the login decided the limit (its credentials for the model are cooling down).

resumeAt.description:

catchUp.description: What to do with a firing missed while the hub was down.

forkBehind.description:

same commands, while these held the same contents, is not set up again. None listed: setup always runs.

runAnyway.description:
True: a failed setup still starts the agent, which is told what failed. False (the default): the start fails,
naming the command and the end of its output.

timeoutSec.description: Each command's time limit, in seconds.

WorktreesKept.description:
The worktrees one nightly cleanup kept in a project because they hold work that exists nowhere else, as one line
that opens to each: what frees it is pushing or deleting that work.
